---
title: Meet standalone Cloudflare release
description: Qualify and publish an exact main commit with a captured rollback pair.
---

Meet can publish independently through `meet-cloudflare.yaml`. A release dispatch
must use the `main` ref and supply its full 40-character commit as `source_sha`.
The workflow rejects a mismatch between that input and `github.sha`; a moving
branch cannot silently select another release candidate.

Build identity acceptance requires the Meet app name, exact source SHA, production
environment, and production ref name. A mismatch reports only allowlisted identity
fields and valid source hashes; arbitrary response bodies are excluded. Compare
that receipt with the sealed artifact before attributing a failure to caching or
propagation. The restored production runtime checks the same identity fields before
publication. A failed promotion restores the captured pair and requires fresh
release authorization before another dispatch or rerun.

## Prepare the release

The existing `meet-production` GitHub environment must permit exactly the
`production` and `main` branches and require approval by `vhpx` before dispatch.
Both the train and standalone deploy jobs use this protected environment. Its
existing secrets remain unchanged. Environment policy changes require the release
authority's approval and execution by the credential custodian. Verify the policy
readback before dispatch; a missing environment must never be auto-created by a
release run. Never copy secret values into logs, command arguments, review packets
or run artifacts.

Record the exact candidate, live-to-candidate source-range review, current release
holds and provider authorization. The candidate must include the accepted startup
and authentication regression fixes. A source review or green build does not
replace the per-dispatch authorization or source-range receipt.

The admission gate requires the latest completed successful run for that exact
main SHA of Types, Security, Test, CodeQL, Oxc and Meet Cloudflare. It excludes the
current release run. A successful Meet workflow whose `validate` job was skipped
by the affected-path gate counts as green for this historical CI predicate. It is
not an emitted-artifact qualification receipt: the release dispatch must execute
its own validation, restored-artifact checks and production-input provenance.

## Dispatch and approve

After the exact commit is on main and the release packet is approved:

```sh
gh workflow run meet-cloudflare.yaml --ref main \
  -f release=true -f source_sha="$SOURCE_SHA"
```

Record the resulting run ID and confirm its `head_sha` matches the approved
candidate. The reviewer approves only that run's pending
`meet-production` deployment, after the release authority issues a provider ACK
naming that run ID and the reviewer checks the candidate. If main advances before dispatch, the SHA equality guard stops the
run; qualify the new candidate instead of changing the input silently.

Both release paths use the fixed `meet-cloudflare-production-deploy` concurrency
group. Admission repeats inside that group before provider operations. For a
production-ref run, live equal to or descended from the source is a successful
no-op with `MEET_RELEASE_SUPERSEDED`; it performs no deployment or success-marker
write. Divergent sources stop with `MEET_RELEASE_DIVERGENT`. A stale standalone
dispatch stops rather than replacing a newer live release.

## Artifacts and rollback

The validate job builds and seals the frontend and realtime output. Realtime's
archive SHA-256 is exported as a validate-job output and checked before extraction
in deploy, independently of the seal inside the archive. Publication uses the
qualified realtime output with `--no-bundle`; Cloudflare credentials are scoped to
provider steps, not dependency installation or compilation.

Before the first publication, capture both currently serving Worker deployment
and version IDs. Each must serve one version at 100 percent. Retain the resulting
`meet-rollback-frontend-target.json` and `meet-rollback-realtime-target.json`
alongside the authorized release receipt. A historical pair alone is insufficient.

The workflow restores both captured versions if publication or smoke checks fail.
With the same captured receipts and approved credential context, the one-command
recovery is:

```sh
bash scripts/ci/meet-release-operations.sh restore
```

The helper verifies both serving versions after restoration. A failed release
remains failed and does not emit a success marker. Retain rollback and admission
results even when the deploy stops.

## Live acceptance

Check `/api/build-info` against the candidate and verify the frontend and realtime
deployment identities. Using a consent-qualified disposable account and an approved
empty meeting, verify opted-in Sorbet, the display-name and email/workspace footer,
login, logout and realtime connection. Do not use another person's signed-in
session for destructive account actions. Missing test custody is blocked/not run,
not a product failure. Capture signed-in navigation and request timings using the
[Meet loading contract](/platform/applications/meet#signed-in-list-loading).
